item.title: Arts Council England: Music Growth Fund, GBP 1,000-40,000 strand
item.description:
Organisation: Arts Council England

Location: England. Supports new music by living, UK-based artists and music creators.

Award: GBP 1,000 to GBP 40,000, from a total annual budget of GBP 3,000,000 for this strand in 2026/27. You must find at least 25 percent of the total project budget as CASH match funding. No application fee.

Duration: Four rounds across 2026/27; the next closes 3 September 2026

Deadline: 03 Sep 2026

The Music Growth Fund is Arts Council England's new investment programme for growth in new music, meaning original live performance, sound recording or musical work recently or newly created or performed by living UK-based artists and music creators. It sits inside the wider GBP 45 million Music Growth Package. WHO IT IS FOR: music festivals, music managers, music promoters, music publishers, record labels, recording studios, rehearsal spaces and grassroots music venues, plus established sector bodies and other sector support organisations that support them. Each applicant type has its own Applicant Specific Guidance on the Music Growth Package pages. IMPORTANT: this is business and organisational investment, not a grant for individual artists to make work. Individual artists, bands, producers and artist collectives should instead look at the separate Music Creators Growth Fund (GBP 10,000-20,000), whose guidance lands 1 September 2026 with the portal opening 1 October 2026. WHAT TO PROPOSE: how investment will be used to grow music businesses and/or the wider music industry, and enhance opportunities for artists and music creators, industry professionals, music fans and new audiences. Growth can mean increased reach, stronger business models, improved sustainability, skills development or expanded capacity, and is judged in the context of each applicant's own scale and ambitions. DECISION CRITERIA: potential for growth, effective use of funds, contribution to a fairer and more inclusive music industry, and contribution to a climate resilient music industry. BEFORE YOU START: you need an approved profile on the Arts Council grants management system before you can submit, so allow time for that. Arts Council reserves the right to change the programme, so check you are on the latest guidance. THIS STRAND: GBP 1,000 to GBP 40,000, with a GBP 3,000,000 annual budget for 2026/27 and a 25 percent cash match requirement. ROUNDS FOR 2026/27 (GBP 1,000-40,000 strand): Round 1 opens 6 August and closes 3 September 2026, decision 28 October. Round 2 opens 4 September and closes 15 October 2026, decision 28 October. Round 3 opens 16 October and closes 26 November 2026, decision 3 February 2027. Round 4 opens 27 November 2026 and closes 7 January 2027, decision 9 March 2027. ROUNDS FOR THE GBP 40,001-100,000 strand: Round 1 opens 7 September and closes 1 October 2026, decision 30 November. Round 2 opens 23 November 2026 and closes 15 January 2027, decision 8 March 2027.

item.title: Ottawa School of Art: Call for Exhibition Proposals 2027-2028
item.description:
Organisation: Ottawa School of Art (OSA)

Location: Ottawa, Ontario, Canada. Two venues: the J.W. Stellick Gallery at the ByWard Market campus, and the OSA Orleans Gallery on the Centrum Level of the Shenkman Arts Centre.

Award: Artists receive an Ontario CARFAC exhibition fee (the amount is not stated in the call and follows the CARFAC schedule). No application fee.

Duration: One exhibition slot in the 2027-2028 exhibition season at one campus gallery.

Deadline: 04 Sep 2026

The Ottawa School of Art invites artists and collectives to submit exhibition proposals for its 2027-2028 season, welcoming current and proposed work across all media including painting, sculpture, photography, installation and video. Group exhibition proposals are accepted. Successful applicants exhibit at ONE campus gallery, but proposals may be submitted for either or both venues; an application to both must demonstrate a clear understanding of how the exhibition would work best within each gallery's dimensions (floor plans are published with the call). VENUES: the J.W. Stellick Gallery at the ByWard Market campus, dedicated to giving OSA students and the community a wide variety of contemporary art, and the OSA Orleans Gallery on the Centrum Level of the Shenkman Arts Centre. Artists receive an Ontario CARFAC exhibition fee. SELECTION: a jury of three art professionals selects exhibitions on the quality of the work, the integrity of the proposal, and its relation to OSA's programs. SUBMISSION: all six components are required, incomplete proposals are withdrawn without notification, and poorly organised proposals will not be reviewed. (1) Completed application cover form with contact information and exhibition details. (2) A written exhibition proposal outlining the concept and intent of the proposed or current body of work. (3) One artist statement per proposal; group proposals submit a single collective statement, not individual statements. (4) An up-to-date CV for the exhibiting artist, or a CV for each participating artist in a group proposal. (5) Up to 10 visual files of work completed within the last two years. An artwork and a detail of the same artwork count as two images; images must be JPG only, 300 dpi, no larger than 2MB each, RGB, maximum 1240 pixels on the longest side. Each video counts as one file, total video time per proposal must not exceed 15 minutes, and videos must be AVI, MOV or MP4 and no larger than 500MB each. Precede each file name with a zero-padded number and the title, for example 01Artwork title. (6) A corresponding numbered visual file list with title, year, medium and dimensions (H x W x D), specifying inches or centimetres. FILES MUST BE SENT VIA WETRANSFER to boutique@artottawa.ca; proposals submitted by post, hand delivery or email will not be accepted. Deadline 4:30 pm ET, Friday 4 September 2026.

item.title: Scuola Piccola Zattere: International Fellowship and Residency 2027 (Venice)
item.description:
Organisation: Scuola Piccola Zattere

Location: Venice, Italy. Open to any nationality.

Award: EUR 5,000 fellowship grant plus a EUR 2,000 research budget, accommodation in Venice, an individual study space within a shared studio, and round-trip travel to Venice. Collectives and duos share a single grant and one accommodation. No application fee.

Duration: Three months, in one of two slots: early January to early April 2027, or mid-April to mid-July 2027. Applicants may name one slot or indicate availability for both.

Deadline: 04 Sep 2026

Scuola Piccola Zattere is an independent non-profit centre for continuous education and research in the expanded field of contemporary arts, running exhibitions, commissions, fellowships, workshops, seminars, performances and public discussions as one connected research ecosystem rather than separate strands. Two international fellowships are offered. The support is unusually solid for a research fellowship: EUR 5,000 as a grant, EUR 2,000 as a research budget, accommodation, travel and a study space for three months. SEASON THEME: the 2026-2027 cycle is titled Living Document, investigating archives, regulatory documents, collective rituals, games, performative instructions, and the relationship between bodies, architecture and social organisation. Fellows join that shared inquiry while continuing their own work, and are expected to keep an active presence in the institution and contribute to public events through workshops, seminars, presentations, screenings or performances. The fellowship overlaps with the run-up to and opening of the 2027 Architecture Biennale, which is a real advantage if your research benefits from that traffic. ELIGIBILITY: artists, curators, researchers, architects, choreographers, performers and writers of any nationality, as individuals, collectives or duos. Good English is required, and non-EU applicants need a valid passport for international travel. No age limit, but the organisers say it is especially intended for practitioners in the post-academic stage of their career, typically under 40. You must be prepared to spend the full period in Venice, so this is not a remote or partial-attendance fellowship. WHAT THEY WANT: an active research process that can develop through discussion and experimentation, tied to the Living Document theme, not a finished stand-alone project proposal. The motivation letter, portfolio and public programming proposal are read as one integrated application. Deadline 4 September 2026 at 10:00 CEST.

item.title: Resilient Futures Call 2026: Ideation Grants (climate resilience and political leadership)
item.description:
Organisation: Better Politics Fund, European Climate Foundation, Naia Trust and the Vibe Fund

Location: Global, with priority countries per region. Cannot fund applicants in a long list of excluded countries, which includes the United States, India, Pakistan, China, Russia and others (full list on the call page).

Award: USD 700,000 total across the whole call (Ideation plus Incubation streams). Ideation Grants: USD 10,000 to USD 20,000. Free to apply. Incubation Grants (up to USD 50,000) are by nomination only and have no application process.

Duration: Not specified; grants support new or early-stage ideas and pilots. Decisions announced late November / early December 2026.

Deadline: 04 Sep 2026

NOTE: this is a climate-and-democracy funder rather than an arts or technology programme; relevance to creative or tech practice depends on whether political leadership is a genuine driver of the proposed model. The Resilient Futures Call is a co-funded initiative by the Better Politics Fund, the European Climate Foundation, Naia Trust and the Vibe Fund supporting non-partisan initiatives working at the intersection of democratic political leadership and climate resilience globally. Total available funding is USD 700,000 across two streams: Ideation Grants (open call, this entry) and Incubation Grants (nomination only, up to USD 50,000, for approaches already proven beyond early testing; nominees are contacted directly and there is no way to apply). WHAT IS FUNDED, across three areas: (1) Pathways, helping climate scientists, advocates and affected communities work more effectively with political and governance decision-makers so that evidence and local knowledge shape policy and policy is carried through at every level of government, from town councils to national parliaments; (2) Leadership, programs integrating a critical climate lens into democratic leadership development, strengthening ethical communication, policy design, implementation and strategic coalition-building, including pipelines for leaders from underrepresented backgrounds; (3) Cross-Sector Leadership, backing leadership on energy, housing, transport, food, security, health and conservation, and helping reform political systems and institutions so leaders and new ideas in these areas can succeed. The funders want work where political leadership is a key driver of change, not a side effect. WHO CAN APPLY: organizations, networks, collectives or individuals anywhere eligible. No need to be a registered charity and no need to be based in a priority country, though it strengthens regional fit. ELIGIBILITY CHECK (all must be yes): the idea is new or early-stage (organization under 12 months old, or a new pilot from an older organization; established programs with a strong track record are not right for an Ideation Grant); it aligns with at least one of the three funding areas and with regional priorities; it is non-partisan (no parties, candidates or campaigns); the applicant is based in an eligible location. PRIORITY COUNTRIES: Africa (Kenya, Nigeria, South Africa); Asia (Bangladesh, Indonesia, Nepal, Philippines, Sri Lanka, Thailand); Europe (France, Germany, Hungary, Italy, Poland, Romania, Spain, UK); Latin America (Argentina, Bolivia, Colombia, Ecuador, Guyana, Peru, Suriname); Pacific (Cook Islands, Federated States of Micronesia, Fiji, Kiribati, Marshall Islands, Nauru, Niue, Palau, Papua New Guinea, Samoa, Solomon Islands, Timor-Leste, Tonga, Tuvalu, Vanuatu). CANNOT FUND, for legal and operational reasons, individuals and organizations in: Afghanistan, Azerbaijan, Bahrain, Belarus, Burkina Faso, China, Cuba, DR Congo, Eritrea, Eswatini, Georgia, Guinea, Guinea-Bissau, Haiti, India, Iran, Jordan, Kuwait, Laos, Libya, Mali, Morocco, Myanmar/Burma, Nicaragua, Niger, North Korea, Oman, Palestine (Gaza), Pakistan, Qatar, Russia, Saudi Arabia, Syria, Sudan, South Sudan, Somalia, Turkmenistan, Uganda, United Arab Emirates, the United States, Uzbekistan, Vietnam, Yemen, and Russian-occupied territories in Ukraine (Crimea, Donetsk, Luhansk, Zaporizhzhia, Kherson). NOT FUNDED: physical infrastructure such as solar panels or climate infrastructure where political leadership is not a driver of the model; research, accountability scorecards and policy-gap mapping (the funders support the leaders and institutions who act on evidence, not the generation of it); public awareness campaigns without a political leadership dimension; anything affiliated with a political party or candidate; corporate sustainability or ESG initiatives; outside-pressure advocacy campaigns that push governments on emissions targets without building new leadership capacity; citizens' assemblies or deliberation projects with no link to political leaders or institutions acting on the outcomes; transparency or open-data initiatives that do not feed into political or institutional decision-making; watchdog or investigative journalism without a direct link to strengthening political leadership or institutional response. ASSESSMENT CRITERIA: innovation (a genuinely new idea, method or audience); impact potential; strategic clarity (a credible plan connecting activities to the intended outcome); financial clarity; regional fit; leadership (motivation, experience and rootedness in local context). PROCESS: fill out the short application form before midnight CET on 4 September 2026. There is no second full proposal stage. Every application is acknowledged; all are screened and shortlisted, and a Grantmaking Council of eight regional experts across Asia, Europe, Latin America, Africa and the Pacific reviews the shortlist and makes recommendations. Shortlisted applicants are asked for supporting documentation for due diligence, sometimes including a short call. Feedback is only given to shortlisted applicants; no reply by December 2026 means the application was unsuccessful. INFORMATION SESSION: online 17 August 2026, two sittings at 8:00 CET and 16:00 CET, registration on the call page. Questions: resilientfutures@betterpolitics.foundation.

item.title: JUGAAD: Absolute Improvisation, open call for printed matter and small-format works (Amsterdam)
item.description:
Organisation: SAC Art Amsterdam and Mama Magnet

Location: Fair takes place 9-10 October 2026 in Amsterdam. Open internationally, but selected work must be shipped to the Netherlands by the end of September 2026 at the artist's expense.

Award: No application fee. Selected work is sold at the printed matter fair on mutually agreeable terms regarding commission, duration and number of editions; artists are remunerated within 30 days of each sale. Unsold works are returned at the end of the agreed consignment period.

Duration: Rolling selection 5 August to 5 September 2026; fair 9-10 October 2026

Deadline: 05 Sep 2026

Open call from SAC Art Amsterdam and Mama Magnet for a printed matter fair themed around jugaad: improvised, resourceful solutions built from what is on hand (from the Sanskrit yuj, 'to join', via Hindi jugar, famously embodied by post-independence Punjabi vehicles pieced together from scrap metal and pump engines). The curators want work that engages the spirit of jugaad either as subject (everyday intelligences of getting by, lateral logics of adaptation, unlikely workarounds, reinvention born of necessity) or in how it was made (found or repurposed materials, adapted processes, structures built to solve a specific constraint). Work that came from adjustment rather than access, problem-solving rather than budget. WHAT: zines, artist books, comics, risograph or photocopied prints, posters, foldables, instruction manuals, packaging and other small-format works; if it can travel in a suitcase it is probably in scope. No framed work or anything needing gallery-standard installation. Gen-AI images and text are not accepted. WHO: artists, designers, writers and collectives whose practice genuinely engages with the theme; if unsure, reach out and explain in a line or two. Selected work must reach the Netherlands by end of September 2026. TERMS: selections made on a rolling basis 5 August to 5 September; selected work is sold at the fair (9-10 October, Amsterdam) on mutually agreeable commission terms, with payment within 30 days of each sale and unsold work returned after the consignment period. HOW TO APPLY: email info@mamamagnet.org with a CC to art@sacartamsterdam.com, subject line 'JUGAAD - [Your Contribution]', by 5 September 2026; earlier is better given rolling selection.

item.title: Erie Canal Museum: Erie Canal Artist-in-Residence 2027
item.description:
Organisation: Erie Canal Museum (with the New York State Canal Corporation)

Location: New York State, USA. Non-residential: there is no live-in accommodation, and the work is fieldwork along the New York State Canal System (524 miles of navigable waterways and 365 miles of multi-use trails) and its communities, with engagement with Canal Corporation and Museum staff and facilities. The Museum is in the 1850 Syracuse Weighlock Building, Syracuse, NY. Finalist interviews are conducted virtually.

Award: USD 10,000 artist stipend per residency, for two Artists-in-Residence. Collectives applying as a group receive one USD 10,000 stipend between them. No application fee. The final project feeds into an exhibit and catalogue, with an exhibit opening in the first half of 2028.

Duration: One year: 1 January to 31 December 2027. Finalist interviews 28 September to 23 October 2026 (virtual); artist notification by 13 November 2026; exhibit opening in the first half of 2028.

Deadline: 06 Sep 2026

The Erie Canal Museum, in partnership with the New York State Canal Corporation, is appointing two Erie Canal Artists-in-Residence for a one-year, year-long creative inquiry into the New York State Canal System, including the historic Erie Canal: reflecting on its past, contemplating its current condition, and considering its future. The 2027 residencies are dedicated to projects that reflect upon the Canal's physical, environmental and social condition and history, its materiality and its context, and the project must directly address the Canal. Applicants propose a specific creative visual project that must be exhibitable in a gallery setting, identify their target audiences and explain how the work will be shared with them and with the public at large. Studies of Canal communities are encouraged, but the Canal and its context must be central. Projects may focus on key areas or on the entire system, and applicants are told to weigh that scale: 524 miles of navigable waterways and 365 miles of multi-use trails. ELIGIBILITY: all artists are encouraged to apply, and special consideration goes to artists with ancestral ties to the Haudenosaunee Confederacy and/or the Mohican Nation and to artists who have lived or worked in Canal communities. Only individual artists or artist collectives may apply; artists representing nonprofit or for-profit organisations may not. Artists must be 18 or older and may not be currently enrolled in school full time. For collectives, only one USD 10,000 stipend is awarded to the group. APPLICATION: a statement of interest and proposal (up to 500 words) covering why the residency interests you, your proposed project and how it meets the three residency goals (engage with the Canal, adjacent Canalway Trails, Canal Corp. and Museum staff, Canal facilities, communities and visitors; reflect directly on the Canal's physical, environmental and social condition and history; consider a fuller, more complete account of the Canal's past, present and future), which geographic section you will focus on, how you would share work publicly during the residency, your proposed final project, and how your previous work and public engagement relate; an artist's statement (up to 300 words); a resume or CV (max three pages); two professional references with phone and email; and ten examples of recent work (written work limited to three pages each) with a list giving title, date, materials and size plus short descriptions. EVALUATION covers clarity and relevance of the proposal, the scope, feasibility and clarity of the plan to reach the intended audience, the plan for public engagement including at least one public-facing event during the residency, a final project usable in an exhibit and catalogue, and the quality and relevance of prior work. Applications are reviewed by a panel of Erie Canal Museum and Canal Corporation representatives plus invited arts professionals (the 2026 panel included Elizabeth Dubben of Collar Works, artist and educator Dennis RedMoon Darkeem, and Garth Johnson, Curator of Ceramics at the Everson Museum of Art); finalists interview with the panel. SUBMIT application packages as PDFs by email to Natalie Stetson, Executive Director, at employment@eriecanalmuseum.org with 'Erie Canal Artist-in-Residence' in the subject line, by 11:59 pm on Sunday 6 September 2026. The RFP is at eriecanalmuseum.org/about/careers/.

item.title: Utrecht University: PhD, Media and Democracy in the 1970s (NWO Vidi project)
item.description:
Organisation: Utrecht University, Faculty of Humanities, Department of History and Art History

Location: Utrecht, Netherlands (Drift 6)

Award: EUR 3,059 to 3,881 gross per month at 36 to 40 hours per week, on the Dutch university PhD scale, plus 8 percent holiday allowance and 8.3 percent year-end bonus. No application fee.

Duration: 18-month initial contract, extended to four years after a positive first-year assessment

Deadline: 06 Sep 2026

Fully funded PhD position in the NWO-funded Vidi project 'Democracy and the (de-)regulation of the media in Europe since the 1970s', which reads the contestation and transformation of democracy in the last quarter of the twentieth century through media governance. This sub-project examines how social movements, pirate broadcasters and alternative media initiatives challenged the public broadcasting monopoly across Western Europe during the long 1970s, drawing on archival research. REQUIREMENTS: a master's degree in history or a related field, a demonstrated interest in the history of democracy and media governance, professional English plus at least one other European language, archival research experience and a collaborative approach. Apply through the AcademicTransfer posting (vacancy number 5535). Project leader Dr Pepijn Corduwener (p.corduwener@uu.nl). Deadline 6 September 2026.

item.title: Accion Cultural Espanola: PICE Movilidad 2026 (Phase 3)
item.description:
Organisation: Accion Cultural Espanola (AC/E)

Location: Anywhere outside Spain, at the applicant's own venue or event. Applicant must be a foreign entity constituted outside Spain.

Award: Max EUR 15,000 per applicant per call, per event and per thematic area; within that, max EUR 5,000 per participant or collective. Total 2026 call budget EUR 1,810,000 (Musica y creacion sonora EUR 320,000, Artes visuales EUR 200,000, Videojuego y animacion EUR 90,000, Arquitectura y diseno EUR 90,000, Podcast EUR 90,000). Mandatory co-financing: the applicant must commit at least 50 percent of each proposal's total budget. No application fee.

Duration: Single event or project; Phase 3 activities must start on or after 1 November 2026 and finish before 28 February 2027.

Deadline: 07 Sep 2026

PICE Movilidad is AC/E's collaboration scheme with foreign cultural institutions: a festival, biennial, museum, venue, gallery or platform OUTSIDE Spain applies for AC/E to cover the costs of programming Spanish or Spain-resident artists, collectives and cultural professionals in its own public programme. This is one of the clearest routes for a non-Spanish festival to have a foreign national fund pay for part of its programme. Ten thematic areas are covered including Artes visuales, Musica y creacion sonora, Podcast, Videojuego y animacion and Arquitectura y diseno, so tech-crossover, sound-art and media-art programming is squarely in scope. For visual arts and architecture/design, covered costs include production materials, purchase or rental of technical equipment, hiring of technicians, curators, coordinators and designers, reproduction and exhibition rights, logistics and transport of works, publications, documentation, accommodation, per diems, travel and insurance; for Musica y creacion sonora coverage is narrower (travel, accommodation, per diems, internal transport). Non-EU and UK organisations are fully eligible; there is no EU-membership requirement. Natural persons are barred. TIMING: Phase 3 closes 7 September 2026, provisional list 21 October, definitive award list 30 October, and Phase 3 projects may not begin before 1 November 2026, so this window cannot retro-fund an event already scheduled for autumn 2026.

Only entities constituted in Spain may apply; natural persons are barred. Invited guests may come from any country including non-EU and the UK. item.title: KNOWCASE Open Call 2027: permanent digital-culture installation in Madrid (Sonar+D x Fundacion Cotec)
item.description:
Organisation: Fundacion Cotec and Sonar+D

Location: Installation at the KNOWCASE storefront of Fundacion Cotec's headquarters in Chamberi, Madrid, Spain, a street-level venue visible 24/7. The call is international; applications accepted in Spanish, other official languages of Spain, or English.

Award: Up to EUR 100,000 (plus VAT), all-inclusive: conceptualisation, design, technical development, production, installation, maintenance, documentation, artist fees, travel, accommodation and insurance.

Duration: Installation displayed for a minimum of 24 months, starting February 2027

Deadline: 07 Sep 2026

Fundacion Cotec (a Spanish innovation-focused non-profit) and Sonar+D, building on an initial experiment at Sonar 2026, invite proposals for a long-term installation at KNOWCASE, the street-level showcase of Cotec's Madrid headquarters in Chamberi, visible to the public 24 hours a day. THEME: digital culture, meaning projects that combine knowledge, research, science and data with art, technology and social impact. Cotec's stated priorities are the big transitions (analogue to digital, linear to circular economy, tangible to intangible) plus innovation ecosystems and R&D&I, the climate crisis, the future of work and learning, social divides, citizen participation and democratic health. WHAT YOU GET: a budget of up to EUR 100,000 plus VAT covering everything (design, production, installation, maintenance, documentation, artist fees, travel, accommodation and insurance), and a minimum 24-month public display from February 2027. WHO CAN APPLY: artists, collectives, designers, technologists, universities, research centres, startups, businesses, creative agencies, producers, cultural institutions and multidisciplinary teams, internationally; applicants must demonstrate solid experience and a relevant portfolio. CONSTRAINTS: the proposal must be original and never previously exhibited, must include participative or interactive elements, must encourage critical thinking, and must be technically and financially viable for the full 24+ month exhibition period (durability and maintenance are central selection criteria). Selection weighs conceptual quality highest (40 percent), followed by public interactivity (25 percent). HOW TO APPLY: one PDF of maximum 15 pages containing summary, concept, technical proposal, visuals, budget, timeline, team profile, portfolio and declaration, in Spanish, another official language of Spain, or English, via the application portal linked from the terms and conditions. Results announced 14 October 2026. Deadline 7 September 2026 at midnight CEST.

item.title: Princeton Arts Fellowship 2027-2029 (Lewis Center for the Arts)
item.description:
Organisation: Princeton University, Lewis Center for the Arts

Location: In person on campus at Princeton, New Jersey, USA. Appointees are expected to be full and active members of the community with frequent, engaged interaction with students. These positions are not eligible for sponsorship of an H-1B visa requiring consular processing.

Award: USD 93,000 salary per year for each of two academic years, as a full-time 24-month appointment at the rank of Associate Professional Specialist. No application fee.

Duration: Two academic years, 2027-2028 and 2028-2029. Applications open 1 July 2026 and close 8 September 2026; finalists attend an on-campus interview during the week of 7 December 2026.

Deadline: 08 Sep 2026

The Princeton Arts Fellowship places early-career artists at the Lewis Center for the Arts for two academic years on a full-time salaried appointment, on the conviction that exposure to the arts helps us make sense of our lives and the lives of our neighbours. ELIGIBLE APPLICANTS are early-career composers, conductors, musicians, choreographers, playwrights, designers, directors and performance artists. IMPORTANT FOR THIS CYCLE: applications are accepted only for the Program in Dance, the Program in Theater and Music Theater, and the Department of Music. Fellows typically teach one undergraduate course per semester (subject to approval by the Office of the Dean of the Faculty), or in some cases take on an artistic assignment with students in lieu of a class; prior teaching experience is NOT required. Beyond that, fellows are expected to engage with the Princeton community through advising students, talks, workshops, exhibitions or other events, and have time to pursue their own artistic practice and scholarly research. NOT ELIGIBLE: the appointment cannot be used to fund work leading to a PhD or any advanced degree; holders of Princeton PhDs cannot apply; past recipients of the Hodder Fellowship cannot apply; and anyone with a sustained and continuous relationship with Princeton is excluded (an occasional and sporadic relationship is fine). Fellows may not hold concurrent teaching positions at other institutions during the appointment. You may apply once per application cycle. APPLICATION via Interfolio: a CV; a 750-word proposal broken into how you would use the fellowship to develop your work (250 words), what you might teach or pursue with undergraduates (250 words), and your approach to building community with people of different backgrounds, experiences, perspectives and artistic practices through your practice, teaching and/or research (250 words); contact information for one reference; and work samples with a 150-word statement on how they relate to your proposal, submitted as links in a PDF. WORK SAMPLE SPECS: Dance (choreography), one to three links to performances, rehearsals or research, continuous footage only, no trailers, photographs or promotional material, with cue points of no more than 3 to 4 minutes per link and no more than 10 minutes total. Music, one to two scores and/or links to performance examples totalling 10 minutes, video optional. Theater, up to 15 pages of writing sample and/or up to 10 design images (photos or renderings) and/or a video or audio reel with cue points, no more than 10 minutes to watch. The deadline is 8 September 2026 at 11:59 pm EDT; receipt of applications cannot be confirmed and late applications are not accepted. FAQ and examples of building community in artistic practice, teaching and research: arts.princeton.edu/fellowships/faq.

Location: Vienna, Austria (VBKÖ exhibition spaces and shared kitchen)

Duration: 4 to 6 weeks, taking place between March 2027 and February 2028

Deadline: 10 Sep 2026

VBKÖ, the Austrian Association of Wom*n Artists founded in 1910, invites proposals for its annual programme running March 2027 to February 2028. The call reads the present moment through the resurgence of authoritarianism, fascism, militarisation, colonial violence and extractive capitalism, and the parallel privatisation of care and criminalisation of solidarity. Drawing on María Galindo's framing of feminism as a project of social transformation and Sara Ahmed's account of feminist work beginning with refusal, the programme treats alternative ways of living as something rehearsed collectively through organising, creating, caring, listening, remembering and struggling. VBKÖ seeks a programme of practices that nurture communal care and build a platform for collective rehearsals: proposals that allow for tenderness, that are not afraid of ugly feelings and different truths, and that explore how contemporary queer and feminist perspectives resonate across artistic, social and political movements. FORMAT REQUIREMENT: only exhibition formats bringing together multiple artists, collectives or collaborative practices are accepted. Solo exhibitions, individual presentations and projects centred on a single artist's work are explicitly not supported. Proposals that activate the exhibition through public programming (screenings, performances, workshops, lectures and other events) are encouraged. Regular opening hours are Fridays and Saturdays 2pm to 6pm; any additional hours must be arranged and staffed by the selected group. The association acknowledges that its own history is marked by violence, exclusion and discrimination on the basis of religion, class, gender, sexuality and ethnicity, and states that it actively opposes all forms of discrimination including trans-exclusionary radical feminism. APPLICATION: a single PDF (max 5MB) with a programme description (max 2 pages, images welcome, English or German, including preferred dates and duration), a CV and biography for every participant (max 1 page each), a financial plan (Fair Pay encouraged), technical requirements, and contact details including email, mobile number and main residence; three high-resolution images of work or exhibition sketches sent within the email or via a download link, labelled with artist name, work title, year and proposal title (video links may be included in the proposal). Send to opencall@vbkoe.org with the subject line 'Open Call + your proposal title'. Incomplete applications will not be considered. A shortlist is compiled by the VBKÖ team and final selections are made by the VBKÖ board with an external jury member experienced in contemporary art, activism and community building; shortlisted applicants may be asked to present to the jury. The call is an invitation into the development process: selected artists get access to the technologies, datasets, interfaces and assumptions that shape these systems while they are still being built. Rather than testing whether the systems work, artists are asked to interrogate why they work the way they do, who they are designed for, what forms of creativity they enable or constrain, and what assumptions about culture, intelligence, authorship, labour, bodies, audiences and society are embedded in them. ELIGIBILITY: aged 14 to 30 at the time of submission, any nationality, race, gender or faith; applicants under 18 need parental consent. item.title: Creative Australia: International Engagement Fund (October 2026 round)
item.description:
Organisation: Creative Australia

Location: International, with a confirmed overseas partner.

Award: AUD 5,000 to 30,000. No application fee. No formal matching requirement, but assessment explicitly weighs diversity and scale of income and co-funding, including earned income, grants, sponsorship and in-kind contributions.

Duration: Activities must not exceed two years from the proposed start date; supported activity must fall between 1 July 2026 and 1 July 2028.

Deadline: 13 Oct 2026

Supports reciprocal international exchange between Australian practitioners or organisations and confirmed overseas partners, which makes it the right instrument for co-hosted convenings, labs and cross-border programme partnerships rather than one-way touring. Supported activity types are creative collaboration and development, cultural exchange and knowledge sharing, and labs and practice-exchange models, mapping closely onto media arts residencies, art-and-science research exchanges and digital culture symposia. Eligible costs include artist fees, travel, accommodation, production expenses, marketing, access costs, and childcare or carer support. International organisations are eligible where the project benefits Australian artists or creative workers, and a confirmed international partner is mandatory and must confirm participation in writing. The reciprocity requirement is substantive: the strongest applications embed mutually beneficial exchange rather than simply presenting an Australian artist abroad. Creative Australia's published assessment feedback notes top-ranked applications foregrounded First Nations self-determined or diasporic-led activity and demonstrated sector-wide impact. It is competitive: 157 eligible applications in the March 2026 round yielded 33 grants, about a 21 percent success rate. Contemporary music practitioners are excluded and directed to Music Australia programmes. Closes 13 October 2026 at 3pm AEDT. WHO CAN APPLY: 'individuals, groups and organisations (including small businesses) may apply to this category.' Individual applicants must be an Australian citizen or permanent resident. A legally constituted entity is not required, so unincorporated groups are eligible.

item.title: Canada Council for the Arts: Arts Across Canada and Abroad, Public Outreach (October 2026 round)
item.description:
Organisation: Canada Council for the Arts

Location: Activities must build audiences and public appreciation of the arts in Canada. Organisations must be incorporated or registered in Canada.

Award: CAD. Minimum and maximum are NOT published publicly; disclosed only in the client portal at arts-services.ca, which requires a login. No application fee. Council funds cannot cover expenses already covered by another revenue source; combined public grants must demonstrate complementarity.

Duration: Project-based; results usually notified within 5 months of the deadline.

Deadline: 14 Oct 2026

Funds activities that build connections between artists and diverse audiences and contribute to public appreciation and enjoyment of the arts in Canada. This is the closest Canada Council fit for running a public programme, a single festival edition, a talks series or audience-facing exhibition programming, as distinct from creating the artwork itself. It is open to arts festivals, presenters and event organisers under the Presenting organization profile, alongside Artistic organizations, Artistic groups and Arts supporting groups, and the profile explicitly includes visual arts festivals, biennials, triennials and quinquennials. Digital arts and new media, media arts, inter-arts, and music and sound art are named among funded practices, so experimental sound art and creative technology programming qualify. IMPORTANT: unlike the Circulation and Touring component, international organisations are NOT eligible for Public Outreach. The Council will not fund projects whose primary focus is educational, therapeutic, recreational or social service delivery, nor fundraising activities or prize and award ceremonies. Deadlines fall twice a year. The related Composite Activities component offers up to 3 years of support for bundled multi-project programmes and may suit a recurring festival arc better.

item.title: Fondazione CRT: Bando Ordinarie 2026, Arte, attivita e beni culturali, Progetti (second session)
item.description:
Organisation: Fondazione CRT (Fondazione Cassa di Risparmio di Torino)

Location: Piedmont and Valle d'Aosta, Italy. The project must be delivered in those regions, but the applicant does not need to be headquartered there.

Award: No published fixed minimum or maximum for the arts strand; grant size is set case by case against the project budget and the applicant's financial capacity. Co-financing is not universally mandated but specific categories carry thresholds (conference and seminar requests above EUR 10,000 are inadmissible without co-financing of at least two thirds of budgeted spend). Across all three areas Fondazione CRT distributed roughly EUR 5.5 million to 349 projects in a single recent Ordinarie session. No application fee.

Duration: Project-based; grant-use period governed by the Regolamento Generale di Erogazione 2026, with extensions of up to 12 months available on request.

Deadline: 15 Oct 2026

The Bando Ordinarie is Fondazione CRT's open, non-thematic route: organisations can request support for initiatives that fit the foundation's statutory aims but do not fall under any of its thematic calls, across three areas of which one is Arte, attivita e beni culturali (branded Meraviglia). It is the right door for public programmes, cultural projects, media and digital-culture initiatives and events that are not live performance, exhibitions, film festivals or restoration. READ THE EXCLUSION LIST CAREFULLY: live performance goes to NoteSipari or Orizzonti L.I.V.E., exhibition-format initiatives and film festivals go to Immagini e Prospettive, heritage restoration goes to BeST, and accessible territorial-showcase events go to Eventi for All, so Ordinarie is the residual arts route. Non-profit entities and institutions operating in the reference territory are eligible, and because the applicant does not need to be headquartered in Piedmont or Valle d'Aosta this is genuinely open to organisations based elsewhere, including non-EU and UK, that run a programme in those regions. The project route has two deadlines: the first was 30 April 2026 and the second session is open 1 July to 15 October 2026 at 15:00 Italian time. Organisations receiving an activity-support grant cannot also benefit from other CRT calls in the same calendar year. Applications are made through rol.fondazionecrt.it.

item.title: Gemeente Den Haag: Arts and Culture Projects Category B (autumn 2026 round)
item.description:
Organisation: Gemeente Den Haag (Municipality of The Hague)

Location: The Hague. Applicant must be active in Den Haag and the project must be publicly accessible there. City-restricted.

Award: EUR 10,000 to 30,000 per application. The municipal culture-budget contribution may not exceed 30 percent of the total project budget, so at least 70 percent co-financing is required. Annual ceiling for the strand is EUR 600,000. No application fee.

Duration: Maximum one year per project.

Deadline: 15 Oct 2026

The larger of The Hague's two municipal project bands and the appropriate route for an organisation running a festival or substantial public programme in the city. Awards range from EUR 10,000 to 30,000 against an annual ceiling of EUR 600,000 for the whole strand. THE CO-FINANCING REQUIREMENT IS SEVERE and is the single most important planning constraint: the municipal culture budget may fund at most 30 percent of the total project budget, so an applicant seeking EUR 30,000 must already have roughly EUR 70,000 secured or plausibly projected elsewhere. Only legal entities may apply; individuals and informal collectives must use Category A instead (EUR 2,000 to 10,000, 70 percent coverage ceiling, next window 1 to 15 September 2026). Professional arts and culture organisations running public projects in music, theatre, dance, film, literature, visual arts or combinations are eligible. The next window opens 1 October and closes at 17:00 on 15 October 2026. TIMING: the decision term is 12 weeks after the window closes, so an October 2026 application is decided around early January 2027 and activity should be scheduled from 2027 onward. Applications are handled through the municipality's subsidy system, which migrated to Easyfunders in April 2026. This scheme is independent of Stroom Den Haag. The underlying regulation runs to 31 December 2028.

item.title: Stimuleringsfonds: Open Call Residency Videotage 2027 (Hong Kong)
item.description:
Organisation: Stimuleringsfonds Creatieve Industrie (Creative Industries Fund NL) in collaboration with Videotage, Hong Kong

Location: Residency takes place at Videotage in Hong Kong. Applicants must be established in the Netherlands, Aruba, Bonaire, Curacao, Saba, Sint Eustatius or Sint Maarten (Kingdom of the Netherlands) and registered in a business register within the Kingdom of the Netherlands.

Award: EUR 5,000 for a two-month residency or EUR 6,500 for a three-month residency, paid by the Creative Industries Fund NL to cover travel, insurance, living expenses, compensation for time invested, and material and transport costs. Accommodation, use of the studio space and facilitation by Videotage are covered directly by the Fund on top of this. No application fee.

Duration: Two or three months in 2027 (spring 2027); state your preferred period in the application.

Deadline: 21 Oct 2026

The Creative Industries Fund NL (Stimuleringsfonds) runs this residency with Videotage, a Hong Kong-based non-profit media arts institution specialising in the promotion, presentation, creation and preservation of moving image and media art in all forms and languages. The Fund is recruiting one Netherlands-based designer, maker or observer working in digital culture to spend two or three months at Videotage's studio space in Hong Kong in 2027, conducting research, broadening their network, developing new work inspired by Hong Kong, and presenting their findings or completed works. The residency encourages crossovers and experimentation, giving the participant space to explore new methodologies, widen their creative practice and produce work that pushes the boundaries of digital culture, with a focus on social and urban dynamics. The 2027 edition takes the technological 'black box' phenomenon as its starting point and invites the resident to respond to that theme within the context of Videotage. ELIGIBILITY: you are an individual designer, maker or observer within the field of digital culture; you are established in the Netherlands, Aruba, Bonaire, Curacao, Saba, Sint Eustatius or Sint Maarten (Kingdom of the Netherlands); you are registered in the business register of the Dutch Chamber of Commerce (KvK) or another business register within the Kingdom of the Netherlands; and you have had a professional practice in the creative industry for at least four years. NOT open to duos, collectives or cooperative ventures, nor to designers and makers who receive a grant during the work period under the Talent Development Grant Scheme, the Open Call Self-taught Designer or the Open Call Emerging Design Practices ABCSSS. Note that accepting this open call means you cannot apply to those schemes and open calls in 2027. FUNDING: EUR 5,000 for two months or EUR 6,500 for three months, covering travel, insurance, living expenses, compensation for time invested and material and transport costs; accommodation, studio use and Videotage's facilitation are covered separately by the Fund. Submit your proposal to the Creative Industries Fund NL by 21 October 2026, 16:00 CEST.

item.title: Perform Europe: Third Open Call for Cross-Border Touring (2026-28 edition)
item.description:
Organisation: Perform Europe (IETM, EFA, Circostrada, European Dancehouse Network, Pearle*, IDEA Consult), co-funded by Creative Europe

Location: Europe-wide; touring must happen in at least 3 Creative Europe countries. The UK is NOT eligible.

Award: Three grant tiers of EUR 15,000, EUR 25,000 or EUR 55,000, plus top-ups of up to EUR 5,000, giving a EUR 60,000 ceiling per partnership. EUR 1.4 million total across at least 25 partnerships, covering up to 100 percent of eligible costs, so no matching funds are needed. TOP-UP RATES: green mobility EUR 400 per person per presentation date; accessibility support EUR 400 per person per presentation date; family top-up EUR 200 per child per presentation date; audience access EUR 800 per presentation date; visa EUR 120 per person needing one; overseas and outermost regions EUR 175 per person per presentation date. No application fee.

Duration: Touring and implementation 1 March 2027 to 31 January 2028 (11 months).

Deadline: 22 Oct 2026

Perform Europe is the EU's dedicated cross-border touring scheme for the performing arts, run by a six-organisation consortium and co-funded by Creative Europe. It funds partnerships of at least three organisations from three different Creative Europe countries to tour a finished performing arts work in at least three countries, with an explicit emphasis on greener, more inclusive and more equitable touring practice. Eligible disciplines are circus, dance, outdoor arts, performance art, puppetry and theatre; LIVE MUSIC AND OPERA ARE EXCLUDED, and production costs for new creations are not covered since the work must already be finished before 1 March 2027. Applicants pick one of three grant tiers with no fixed criteria per tier, and may request up to EUR 5,000 in top-ups for accessibility and sustainability measures. Five percent of the total fund is ring-fenced for proposals involving Ukrainian partners or supporting the Ukrainian performing arts sector. All 41 Creative Europe countries are eligible, including Albania, Armenia, Bosnia and Herzegovina, Georgia, Iceland, Kosovo, Liechtenstein, Moldova, Montenegro, North Macedonia, Norway, Serbia, Tunisia and Ukraine, but the UK is not. TIMING: applications close 22 October 2026 at 23:59 CEST, selected partnerships are announced in January 2027, and activity may only start from 1 March 2027. A Matchmaking Platform with over 2,300 registered professionals is available for finding partners before applying. CORE PRIORITY: each partnership must pick either diversity and inclusion or the fight against climate change as its core priority, and must also include measures addressing the other one; that choice has to run visibly through the whole application rather than sit in one section. WHO COUNTS AS A PARTNER: both organisations and individual professionals are eligible, so a partner can be an artist, collective, company, producer, presenter, venue, festival, residency, educational institution or NGO. Eligibility is decided by where you are legally based. The partnership appoints a lead partner who submits, signs and receives the grant. ELIGIBLE COSTS: artistic fees and salaries, travel, accommodation, subsistence, administration, reporting, communication, translation, surtitling, equipment transport, copyright fees, access and environmental measures, complementary activities and capacity building. Venue and equipment rental or purchase is capped at 5 percent of the requested grant, and preparation costs for presenting an existing work at 10 percent. PAYMENT: 60 percent after signing, 20 percent after the first narrative and financial report is approved, and the final 20 percent after completion and EU approval of Perform Europe's own final report. Top-ups are reimbursed only after the project ends and documentation is approved, so budget for the cash-flow gap. PRACTICAL: every partner must register for a Perform Europe account before submission and approval can take several working days, so do not leave that to the last week.

item.title: Stichting NORMA: NORMA Fonds Project Grant (round 4, 2026)
item.description:
Organisation: Stichting NORMA (collecting society for performing artists)

Location: Netherlands-based arts-sector activity. No city or region restriction stated.

Award: Maximum EUR 10,000 per project. Total project budget may not exceed EUR 150,000 and the applicant organisation's annual budget may not exceed EUR 500,000. At least 25 percent of the project budget must come from audience or box-office revenue. Performer fees must meet the 2026 wage norms of EUR 139 per rehearsal and EUR 340 per performance. No application fee.

Duration: Single project, typically a production or concert series. Final report due within six months of completion.

Deadline: 30 Oct 2026

The NORMA Fonds redistributes copyright remuneration collected by Stichting NORMA into cultural, social and professional projects involving performing artists, and is one of the few Dutch schemes with four intakes a year and a genuinely short cycle. Both arts-sector organisations and individual arts professionals may apply, though the applicant needs a bank account and legal footing and cannot be a BIS-funded institution. The project must centre on performing artists in the copyright sense, meaning people who perform a copyright-protected work: musicians, dancers, actors, voice actors. This fits live experimental music, sound performance and performative media-art work, but not object-based exhibitions or non-performative installation programmes. The maximum grant is EUR 10,000, the total project budget must stay under EUR 150,000, the applicant's annual budget under EUR 500,000, and at least a quarter of the project budget must be earned from audience income, so this is a top-up rather than a primary funding source. Budgets must honour NORMA's 2026 performer wage norms. Applications are submitted online during a one-month window each quarter; the next round runs 1 to 30 October 2026, closing at 23:59. TIMING RULE: decisions arrive no later than eight weeks after the deadline, and the premiere date must fall at least eight weeks after the application deadline. Organisations that already received a NORMA Fonds grant in 2024 or 2025 are excluded, and supporting staff may not exceed 2 FTE.

item.title: Sixi International Artist-in-Residence Project 2027 (Nanjing, China)

Duration: Residency period concludes with an exhibition of outcomes

Deadline: 15 Nov 2026

Launched in 2024 to support young emerging artists, the Sixi International Artist-in-Residence Project (run by Sixi Museum in Nanjing, China) facilitates exchanges between artists from different backgrounds and helps them achieve creative breakthroughs and personal growth. The project calls for artists across all disciplines and cultural backgrounds who are ready to engage in dialogue with the city. TWO THEMES FOR 2027: 'Flux and Imprints: Contemporary Echoes of Migration History' and 'Folds of Text: Cross-Media Intertextuality and Intervention'. WHAT IS PROVIDED: living and working space (a city-centre apartment plus a loft studio in the outskirts to suit the research and production demands of different disciplines), financial support, hardware facilities and staff assistance, and help establishing contacts with the local art scene; by the end of the residency artists have the opportunity to showcase their outcomes in exhibitions. Nanjing combines traditional and contemporary Chinese culture, and the project positions itself as one of the few local art residency programmes contributing to international cultural exchange in the city and to the diversified development of contemporary Chinese art. ELIGIBILITY: open to artists across all disciplines and cultural backgrounds. Deadline: 15 November 2026. Apply via siximuseum.com.

item.title: The Japan Foundation: Exhibitions Abroad Support Program (FY2027-28 round)
item.description:
Organisation: The Japan Foundation

Location: Exhibition takes place at the applicant institution's own venue outside Japan. National rounds run through Japan Foundation offices worldwide.

Award: No published ceiling. Partial-cost grant only: packing and shipping of Japanese exhibits (insurance excluded), catalogue production including digital catalogues, and travel for invited Japanese artists, curators and specialists. Preliminary research and development explicitly excluded. The grant is partial by design, so the host institution funds the balance. No application fee.

Duration: Exhibitions must open between 1 April 2027 and 31 March 2028; results notified April 2027.

Deadline: 01 Dec 2026

The Japan Foundation's flagship grant for organisations abroad mounting an exhibition introducing Japanese art and culture, explicitly covering overseas biennials and triennials that present Japanese artists. It is a partial-cost grant rather than a production budget: it pays toward shipping Japanese works, producing print or digital catalogues, and bringing Japanese artists, curators and specialists to the venue. That cost structure suits media arts, digital culture and art-and-science exhibitions well, where shipping technical work and hosting the artist for installation are the main cost drivers. It is explicitly designed for non-Japanese applicants: museums, galleries and comparable organisations outside Japan. Institutions only, so independent curators and artists cannot apply directly and must be hosted by an eligible institution. Exhibition content must introduce Japanese art and culture, so a Japanese artistic component is mandatory. Recent UK recipients include Tate Modern, the V&A and the Hayward Gallery, so the scheme skews toward established institutions. Applicants are asked to discuss eligibility with the relevant regional arts programme officer before applying. FLAG: full FY2027 guidelines were not yet published by Tokyo headquarters as of July 2026 and this deadline is the funder's own provisional date; reconfirm in autumn 2026.
